correctness.rationale: Computing e=F(1), every idempotent is 0, 1, or has scalar part 1/2 and B(w,w)=1/4. In the third case its Peirce-one space is exactly its line, by the vector equations x=2bw and u=2bv for an element with scalar b. Multiplicativity would then express the rank-m pure-vector form as the square tensor of a scalar character, impossible for m≥2. For a unital map write its pure-vector image as phi(v)1+T(v). If phi(v) is nonzero, the vector equation with v=v gives Tv=0 and its equation with arbitrary x gives Tx=0. The scalar equation then gives the same rank contradiction. To justify the quotient argument without assuming that T preserves the radical, first project T restricted to W back to W: the scalar identity shows this map is an isometry and hence surjective. Pairing the W-projection of T(R) against that entire W then forces T(R)⊆R. This gives the stated normal form and its converse, rank, composition and automorphisms. Squaring gives G=I, U²=U, US=0; radical change of basis and conjugating by a shear with T=−S yield one orbit per allowed rank. For a retraction choose a j-plane, one of q^(j(r−j)) complements, and S into that complement. For arbitrary U choose image, kernel and quotient isomorphism independently. Over the algebraic closure the complementary pairs form an open subvariety of the product of Grassmannians; the allowable shears are a vector bundle. The rank-j locus among projections is closed by rank(U)≤j and rank(I−U)≤r−j, avoiding trace ambiguities in positive characteristic. The zero map and unital locus are disjoint closed sets distinguished by F(1). This confirms all component dimensions. Finally the Gaussian-binomial product bounds the rank weights by constant multiples of q^((r−j)(m+2j)); completing the square and using the nearest admissible integer to j_* proves the stated tail bound, including r=m/2.
residual_risks: The geometry conclusion is for the reduced variety only, and no assertion about the nonreduced homomorphism scheme or rank-one/characteristic-two variant is needed.

value.rationale: The result determines exactly where rank may be lost on a natural degenerate form algebra, quantifies its retractions and identifies their conjugacy and algebraic strata. In particular it explains why the retraction counts lose all Witt dependence even though the endomorphism counts retain it, and why typical retractions at large radical dimension do not have either extreme rank. Those structural and distributional facts go beyond recounting a single finite example.
residual_risks: No application to arbitrary radical Jordan extensions, full conjugacy of nonidempotents, or scheme-level deformation classification is asserted.
